summary.suggested: The St. Louis Post-Dispatch reported that Tom Allen, who seconded Artie Flint in his loss to Hugh McManus near St. Clair, Mo., said Flint ignored his advice, proved a quitter, and forced Allen to throw up the sponge.

metadata.notes: Masthead: St. Louis Post-Dispatch, Tuesday, April 17, 1888, page 8.

facts.fact: Allen seconded Artie Flint in his prize fight against Hugh McManus near St. Clair, Missouri; Flint lost and Allen threw up the sponge
places: near St. Clair, Franklin County, Missouri

facts.fact: Allen said Flint lost by ignoring his advice to stay in his own corner
facts.quote: I kept telling him to stay in his corner, not to go out over to the other man's and that he'd win but, no, he knew more about it than I did and he got licked.
No, sir, Flint showed himself to be a quitter, and I had to throw up the sponge.

notes: The quote 'Well, we won the fight' is Tom Kelly's, not Allen's. The fight was reached by excursion train from St. Louis.
